name: Acute Myeloblastic Leukemia with Maturation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of ≥20% myeloblasts in bone marrow or peripheral blood
Evidence of myeloblastic leukemia with maturation showing differentiation beyond the myeloblast stage
Immunophenotypic confirmation of myeloid lineage (e.g., CD13, CD33 positivity)
Detection of recurrent genetic abnormalities associated with AML (e.g., t(8;21)(q22;q22))

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: ≥20% myeloblasts in bone marrow or blood with evidence of maturation beyond myeloblast stage
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other acute leukemias and myelodysplastic syndromes.

pathognomonic.notes: Presence of immature myeloid cells in peripheral blood
searchTerms: high immature white blood cells in blood

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bone marrow hypercellularity with myeloblastic proliferation
searchTerms: overcrowded bone marrow with immature cells
excessive immature white cells in marrow

common.symptomName: Anemia-related pallor and dyspnea on exertion
searchTerms: pale skin and shortness of breath

common.symptomName: Thrombocytopenia causing petechiae and easy bruising
searchTerms: low platelets causing small red spots
petechiae and bleeding from low platelets
frequent infections due to low white cells

common.symptomName: Fever due to infection or leukemic process

occasional.symptomName: Bone pain due to marrow expansion

rare.symptomName: Central nervous system involvement with neurological deficits
searchTerms: nerve deficits due to CNS involvement
lung problems from blood cell buildup

laboratory: Bone marrow biopsy with hypercellularity and myeloblastic proliferation
imaging: Chest X-ray may show leukostasis-related pulmonary infiltrates
Ultrasound or CT for hepatosplenomegaly assessment
other: Immunophenotyping confirming myeloid lineage markers (CD13, CD33, MPO)
Coagulation profile to assess for DIC

distinguishingFeatures: Lymphoid rather than myeloid lineage markers
Less than 20% blasts in bone marrow
Chronic course rather than acute presentation

redFlags: Signs of leukostasis (respiratory distress, neurological symptoms)
references: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues, 2016
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, 2018
Orphanet: Acute Myeloblastic Leukemia with Maturation (ORPHA:98834)
